biology: Biology integrates ecosystem dynamics, genetics (genotype-phenotype relationships, inheritance patterns), cellular structure and function, species taxonomy, photosynthesis, and plant reproduction. It examines ecological interactions, genetic mechanisms, taxonomic classification, trophic roles, adaptive traits, and morphological specialization across organisms, including inherited disorders and reproductive strategies.
physics: Physics addressing thermal and kinetic energy-temperature dynamics, mechanics of force and motion with Newton's third law, states of matter and material properties, and magnetic interactions. Integrates energy transfer, material behavior, and fundamental force principles.
chemistry: Chemistry encompasses elementary substances, compounds, and their molecular structures, focusing on concentration dynamics in solutions, physical and chemical changes, and reaction mechanisms. Core areas include oxidation, acid-base reactions, diffusion, equilibrium, and transformations driven by thermal, environmental, and biological factors, alongside synthesis, decomposition, catalysis, and redox processes.
earth-science: Earth science integrates mineral and rock classification, plate tectonics, atmospheric composition, and paleontological methods for fossil age determination. It encompasses weather-climate distinctions, sedimentary processes, geodynamic phenomena, climatological measurements, planetary composition, and natural resource energy applications.
economics: Economics examines resource allocation through opportunity cost, trade and barter systems, and supply-demand dynamics. It analyzes goods and services, emphasizing how production processes and destruction events influence supply, shaping market equilibrium and exchange value across economic systems.
